source: Standard geometry drawings RDM/1/3/2/01 (Junction type A) and RDM/1/3/2/02 (Junction types B, C & D), Jan 2024; markings to RDM 6.1 (2025) Chapters 5 and 7
note: Islands and markings for the user to place at a junction. Shapes follow the drawn dimensions where the sheets give them and are indicative elsewhere (the sheets are marked 1:500 but are not to scale). The control radii, entry widths W1/W2 and kerb lines come from the junction design, not from these templates: place a piece, then scale it, or move it, to fit. Kenya drives on the left: the approach lane of the minor road is on the right of a person looking up the minor road from the main road.

A-1.name: Junction type A-1 with two islands

A-2.name: Junction type A-2 with additional island

B-Mod.name: Junction type B, modified (ghost island on the main road)
B-Mod.remark: The sheet is titled types B, C and D but labels no panel D: two panels read 'Type B - Modified'. Both are drawn alike and are one template here.

TM07.name: GIVE WAY line, 600 / 300 mm, 400 mm wide

BM07.name: Triangular GIVE WAY marking, 3.75 x 1.1 m

LM24.name: Continuous centre line, 100 mm (barrier line on the minor road)

KERB.name: Raised island, kerbed (kerb faces marked black / white 500 mm, RDM 6.1 12)

GUIDE.name: Construction guide (not marked on the road)

LM05.name: Bus bay separation line, 1 m / 1 m (white)

LM03.name: Broken lane line 2 m / 6 m, 100 mm (white)

ghost_island.name: Ghost island tail on the main road (hatched, yellow)
ghost_island.remark: Beyond the junction for the traffic turning right into the minor road; the right-turn lane length and the main-road widening come from the junction design (RDM 1.3 Fig 9.37).

ghost_lead.name: Hatched strip ahead of the right-turn lane (yellow)

splitter_a1.name: Splitter island, type A-1 (raised 7.5 x 3.0 m, R 1.5, hatched tail)

splitter_a2.name: Splitter island, type A-2 (raised teardrop, hatched tail, about 25 m)

splitter_teardrop.name: Splitter island, types B / C (teardrop 10 + 10 m, R 0.75)

corner_hatch.name: Hatched lead-in to the corner island (white)

give_way_line.name: GIVE WAY line across the approach lane (TM07)
give_way_line.remark: Across the approach lane from 'inner' (the splitter island's edge) to the kerb.

minor_centre_line.name: Continuous centre line on the minor road, 30 m (LM24)

guides.name: Guide lines: main edge, minor centreline and edges, kerb returns, Rc turning arcs
guides.remark: Construction only: no quantities. Kerb returns are single-radius fillets (RDM 1.3 Fig 9.25 uses R1:R2:R3 = 2:1:3 three-centred curves, R2 8-12 m); Rc arcs are tangent to the main-road centreline and pass through the splitter nose; Rc is the control radius, 15 m recommended (RDM/1/3/2/01 note 1).

bus_bay.name: Bus bay (RDM/1/3/3/01)
bus_bay.remark: Entry taper A = 30 m, 25 m where the speed limit is 50 km/h or less; bay B as clicked (25 m for more than one bus); exit taper C = 18 m; 4.0 m deep; 1.0 m raised platform; flush kerbs on the tapers, raised along the bay with 2 m ramped kerbs. Bays serving opposite directions at least 60 m apart, centre to centre.

climbing_lane.name: Climbing lane (RDM 1.3 6.6, RDM/1/3/3/02)
climbing_lane.remark: Tapers of 100 m; full width to where trucks are back within 15 km/h of their level speed, at least 200 m past the crest to merge; lane as wide as the adjacent through lane, which is reduced by 0.25 m where 3.25 m or more (RDM 1.3 6.6.3).
